{
  "name": "dotnet-pilot",
  "displayName": "DotnetPilot",
  "version": "3.7.0",
  "description": ".NET development plugin for Claude Code — Roslyn semantic analysis, DI/architecture/EF Core guards, convention-aware scaffolding, TDD agents, security and performance review, and project lifecycle commands.",
  "author": {
    "name": "Nick Zdanovych",
    "email": "zdanovichnick@gmail.com"
  },
  "homepage": "https://github.com/zdanovichnick/dotnet-pilot",
  "repository": "https://github.com/zdanovichnick/dotnet-pilot",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": [
    "dotnet",
    "csharp",
    "agents",
    "quality-gates",
    "ef-core",
    "aspnet",
    "clean-architecture",
    "roslyn",
    "mcp-roslyn"
  ],
  "mcpServers": "./.mcp.json",
  "types": "./types/index.d.ts",
  "userConfig": {
    "build_status": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Build failure toasts",
      "description": "Show a toast after 3 and 5 consecutive dotnet build/test failures (requires a Claude Code build with mods).",
      "default": true
    },
    "routing": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Routing roster in system prompt",
      "description": "Add the dotnet-pilot routing guidance to the system prompt once per session in .NET projects (requires a Claude Code build with mods).",
      "default": true
    },
    "pressure": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Pressure meter",
      "description": "Score repeated red dotnet runs, re-edits and corrections 0–100 in the status line, warn on test edits that loosen a test after a red run, and add a short system-prompt section while the score is high (requires a Claude Code build with mods).",
      "default": true
    },
    "pressure_test_guard_block": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Block loosening test edits under high pressure",
      "description": "Deny an Edit that skips, removes or comments out a test assertion while the pressure score is 60 or higher. Off by default; the warning toast shows regardless.",
      "default": false
    },
    "pixel_city": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Pixel city band",
      "description": "Draw an animated pixel-art band above the prompt in the terminal: a city, beach, running dinosaur or time-lapse sunset under a day/night sky that reacts to tool activity, with a storm on a failed dotnet build/test and a rainbow when it goes green. /city controls it (requires a Claude Code build with mods).",
      "default": false
    },
    "pixel_city_scene": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Pixel band scene",
      "description": "The scene the pixel band starts with: city, beach, dino (a running T-rex that jumps the cacti; meteors instead of rain in a storm) or sunset (a time-lapse sunrise-to-sunset over mountains and a lake). /city <scene> switches it for the session.",
      "options": [
        "city",
        "beach",
        "dino",
        "sunset"
      ],
      "default": "city"
    }
  }
}
